nodes.label: Shared Supabase Schema in supabase/
nodes.rationale: The schema is shared by web and mobile, and this repo is the only place migrations are written, so the two apps cannot diverge at the database level.

nodes.label: profiles.id IS auth.users.id
nodes.rationale: Everyone owns their own account, so making profiles.id the auth user id keeps every RLS policy a direct comparison against auth.uid() instead of a subquery.

nodes.label: Four Tables: profiles, offers, connections, messages
nodes.rationale: One offer per person is enforced by `unique (user_id)`. Keeping the offer separate from the person is what gives location somewhere natural to live.

nodes.label: discover(search_plz, radius_km) Database Function
nodes.rationale: One database function does role, published, not-already-connected and the distance maths. Web and mobile call the same thing, so neither app contains distance arithmetic and the two cannot drift apart.

nodes.label: cube + earthdistance Instead of PostGIS
nodes.rationale: One question, a few lines, a GiST index - and resolving the postal code locally from a shipped table means no geocoding service: no API key, no rate limit, and nothing that can fail on presentation day.

nodes.label: postal_codes Table (GeoNames, CC BY 4.0)
nodes.rationale: German postal code data from GeoNames under CC BY 4.0, so attribution must be kept in the README and the legal notice. It lives in a migration rather than seed.sql because production needs it and seed.sql never runs against the live database. Codes with several villages collapse to the mean point (hence approximate 'ca. 3 km'), and bulk-mail codes belonging to single companies are excluded because nobody lives at one and GeoNames points them at the administering city - 10875 would have searched Stuttgart.

nodes.label: Postal-Code Centroid, Never a Street Address
nodes.rationale: A radius filter is trilaterable: probe it from three positions and you recover whatever is stored. Because what is stored is a postal-code centroid, the most anyone can recover is the postal area the user already chose to disclose - which matters for an app whose purpose is sending a stranger to an elderly person's front door. discover_feed does not select coordinates at all; distance sorting must be computed server-side and returned as a rounded band.

nodes.label: Row Level Security as the Real Boundary
nodes.rationale: RLS is on for every table and is the boundary - not the UI and not proxy.ts. Read supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql top to bottom before touching a policy; the reasoning is in the comments. Run `npm run db:test` after changing any policy, helper or trigger.

nodes.label: Never Use the service_role Key
nodes.rationale: It bypasses RLS entirely and would turn a public anon key into a public database. If a query returns nothing, the policy is telling you something - fix the query, not the client.

nodes.label: Anon/Publishable Key Is Not a Credential
nodes.rationale: It names the project and nothing else, so it is safe in the client bundle and in a public repo - but only because RLS is on for every table. .gitignore ignores .env* except .env.example; config.toml is committed and uses env(RESEND_API_KEY) substitution so it never holds a literal secret.

nodes.label: Server Actions Are Reachable POST Endpoints
nodes.rationale: proxy.ts does not protect them, so every action in src/lib/actions/ re-reads the session itself.

nodes.label: SECURITY DEFINER Helpers Wrapped in (select ...)
nodes.rationale: Helpers in the private `app` schema are always called as `(select app.foo())` so Postgres evaluates them once per statement instead of once per row.

nodes.label: One Round Trip Per Screen
nodes.rationale: Every list screen is a single query. Fetching a list and then looping for related rows is the thing the two security_invoker views exist to prevent.

nodes.label: discover_feed View
nodes.rationale: security_invoker view (migration 0002_views.sql) returning published cards of the opposite role you are not already connected to; deliberately does not select coordinates.

nodes.label: connection_overview View
nodes.rationale: Per connection: the other person's card, the last message and an unread count, built with LATERALs rather than aggregates over a join.

nodes.label: Next.js 16 Breaking Changes
nodes.rationale: This is not the Next.js most tutorials describe; the bundled docs in node_modules/next/dist/docs/ are the authority. cookies(), headers(), params and searchParams are async; revalidateTag takes a required second argument, with updateTag and refresh new; dynamic/revalidate/fetchCache segment exports no longer exist under Cache Components.

nodes.label: proxy.ts Replaces middleware.ts
nodes.rationale: Exports `proxy`, Node runtime, not configurable, and must sit beside app/ (src/proxy.ts, not the repo root). In the wrong place it silently does not run: pages still render and the only symptom is sessions quietly stopping refreshing an hour in.

nodes.label: cacheComponents and Partial Prerendering
nodes.rationale: The shell prerenders and loads instantly while anything reading the session streams in behind <Suspense>. Only the signed-in user's own profile is cached, via 'use cache: private', keeping it in the browser and never on a server. A Supabase query must never go behind a plain `use cache`: it cannot read cookies, so the only way to make it work would be a service-role client, which disables RLS. Discover, connections and chat stay dynamic - slow and correct beats fast and leaking.

nodes.label: Realtime Chat and setAuth on Token Refresh
nodes.rationale: Clients subscribe to postgres_changes on messages filtered by connection_id, with RLS enforced per subscriber. supabase.realtime.setAuth() must be called when the token refreshes or the channel silently stops delivering after an hour.

nodes.label: Migrations, Not the Dashboard, Are the Source of Truth
nodes.rationale: Schema written in the dashboard is invisible to review, never reaches the generated types the mobile app depends on, and is silently destroyed by the next `supabase db push`. Exploring there is fine, but write the result as a migration before anyone builds on it.

nodes.label: Cloud Database Deliberately Not Seeded
nodes.rationale: seed.sql is committed to a public repo, so seeding the cloud would put five accounts with a published password on the internet. Demo accounts exist locally only, and email confirmations (enable_confirmations) are off locally so those demo logins work without an inbox - turn them on before real use.

nodes.label: Local Demo Accounts and Mail Catcher
nodes.rationale: lena@, tariq@, ingrid@, werner@, elisabeth@ at linde.test all share password linde1234; local mail lands in Inbucket/Mailpit on localhost:54324.

nodes.label: Resend SMTP Configuration
nodes.rationale: SMTP is configured for Resend in config.toml but disabled locally so mail goes to Mailpit and demo accounts work without an inbox. For cloud, set SMTP in the Supabase dashboard (smtp.resend.com:587, user resend, password = API key) rather than in the committed file; Resend needs the sending domain verified.

nodes.label: database.types.ts as the Cross-App Contract
nodes.rationale: src/lib/supabase/database.types.ts is generated and committed as the type-level contract between web and mobile; copy it into linde-mobile after any schema change. Mobile additionally needs AsyncStorage for session persistence and the same setAuth() call on token refresh.

nodes.label: Local Development Setup
nodes.rationale: Node 20+ plus a container runtime for local Supabase; db:start, db:reset, db:test and db:types are the four scripts that matter, with db:types regenerated after every schema change.

nodes.label: linde-mobile Companion App
nodes.rationale: Separate repo consuming the same schema and generated types; it writes no migrations of its own.
